title: Air India Frankfurt-Delhi Flight Diverted to Jaipur After Bomb Threat, Squawk 7500 Alert
excerpt: Flight AI2030, a Boeing 787-9, made an emergency landing at Jaipur International Airport on Wednesday morning and was taken to an isolation bay for security checks. Air India's official comment was awaited.
body:
• Air India flight AI2030 from Frankfurt to Delhi was diverted to Jaipur on Wednesday, October 14, following a bomb threat, according to sources cited by The Hindu and PTI.
  • The Boeing 787-9 made an emergency landing at Jaipur International Airport and was taken to an isolation bay for security checks.
  • A source said the pilot transmitted Squawk Code 7500 — the transponder code for unlawful interference — while the aircraft was in the Mumbai Flight Information Region.
  • The number of passengers on board was not immediately known, and an official comment from Air India was awaited.

An Air India aircraft flying from Frankfurt to Delhi was diverted to Jaipur on Wednesday morning following a bomb threat, according to sources cited by The Hindu. The flight, AI2030, operated with a Boeing 787-9, made an emergency landing at Jaipur International Airport and was taken to an isolation bay for security checks.

Assistant Commissioner of Police, Malviya Nagar, Shiv Dayal told PTI that airport authorities had informed police about the emergency landing of the Frankfurt-Delhi flight following a bomb threat. Further details were awaited, he said. Police sources said security personnel were checking the aircraft in the isolation bay.

The 7500 alert

One source, citing initial information, said the pilot pressed Squawk Code 7500 when the aircraft was in the Mumbai Flight Information Region. Squawk 7500 is the internationally recognised transponder code signalling unlawful interference with an aircraft — the category that covers a hijack alert — and it triggers an immediate security response on the ground, including diversion to an airport where the aircraft can be isolated and searched.

"The flight, AI2030, operated with a Boeing 787-9, made an emergency landing at Jaipur International Airport and was taken to an isolation bay for security checks."

That sequence explains the shape of Wednesday's response: an unscheduled landing at Jaipur rather than a continuation to Delhi, the aircraft parked away from the terminal in an isolation bay, and police and security personnel conducting checks before any decision on the flight's onward journey.

What is not yet known

Details about the number of passengers on board could not be immediately ascertained, and an official comment from Air India was awaited at the time of publication. The nature and origin of the threat — and whether the security checks found anything — had not been disclosed by authorities.

What to watch

Passengers booked on AI2030 or connecting through Delhi should check their flight status with Air India before travelling to the airport, as a diverted long-haul aircraft and its crew typically disrupt the return rotation as well. This story will be updated when Air India or Jaipur airport authorities issue a statement.
